name: Tapestry VC
identity_check: Confirmed as Tapestry VC (tapestry.vc; LinkedIn /company/tapestryvc), the early-stage firm Patrick Murphy (ex-Goldman Sachs, ex-Universal Music fund) founded in 2018 with Web Summit co-founder David Kelly to back repeat founders across Europe and the US. Team in London, San Francisco and Dublin; its first fund was named Amaranthine Fund I. Not Tapestry, Inc. (the fashion group), not Tapestry Networks, and not other funds using 'Tapestry' in their name.

thesis_text.value: Early-stage fund that backs repeat founders, people building their second or third company, at pre-seed and seed across Europe and North America. Sector-agnostic, spanning software, AI, cybersecurity, fintech, autonomy and deep tech. Fund III leads or co-leads seed rounds with $1-3M checks, about a dozen deals a year, with roughly half the portfolio UK-related.

values: London: Fund III coverage (Jul 2026) says Tapestry opened a London office and Murphy relocated there from San Francisco to head the fund
'The London and San Francisco-based' firm (tech.eu, Jul 2026); 'London-based Tapestry VC' (Crunchbase News, Jul 2026)
San Francisco: Murphy's bio on tapestry.vc still says 'when at home in San Francisco'; the firm's first office was near South Park, SF (Murph Capital)
conflicts.reason: The managing partner moved to the new London 'flagship office' in July 2026 and Fund III must be roughly half UK-related. The firm still operates in SF, Dublin and London; no registered address was found.

conflicts.chosen: Fund II = $31M, dated 2022-08-03 (announcement of the second close)
conflicts.reason: The 2022 press is contemporaneous and gives the split ($31M + $20M opportunity fund); the 2021 date may refer to when most commitments came in.

open_items: Fund I (Amaranthine Fund I) final size and close date not published; Murph Capital cites only a $25M target, and Web Summit put $2M into it (Irish Times 2022).

No application form or pitch URL: the site's 'Interested in partnering with us?' form only collects an email address, so application_url is left out; cold inbound marked yes on that basis. Murph Capital describes mostly proactive sourcing.

Nothing found on investing in Indian founders or on requiring a US entity. Portfolio spans Slovenia (Sunrise), Canada (Relay) and the UK, and Fund III's British Business Bank commitment requires roughly half the portfolio to be UK-related.
portfolio_count_reported (40) is the Aug 2022 figure; no newer count published. The site's portfolio page lists 16 companies.
A startupmag.co.uk page headlined 'Tapestry closes £60m fund for UK scale-ups' returned only its headline; it could not be tied to Tapestry VC and was not recorded.
SEC EDGAR / Companies House not checked for fund legal names.

Portfolio rounds seen but not recorded because no fetched round page names Tapestry: Keycard $8M seed + $30M Series A (Oct 2025; Upstarts Media, SiliconANGLE and Biometric Update name only a16z, boldstart, Acrew and angels), Manna Series B (Apr 2026; Fortune names ARK, ISIF, Schooner, Coca-Cola HBC, Molten). Not fetched: Nothing's $200M raise (FT, paywalled), BBC 'Deal moves software firm closer to $1bn unicorn status' (Apr 2026, fetch blocked), Requesty coverage on Business Insider (blocked), Ladder Series A (Tapestry named as a Series A lead in the 2024 release, but the round's own page was not found), Loctax, Corner, Ichi, Cloudsmith, Crossbeam, Zapp, Hopin, Nothing seed.
Every card on tapestry.vc/portfolio carries an 'Exit' tag, including live companies, so it is treated as a site filter label rather than exit status.
